newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus leader picks loyalists to head courts.
newsitem.headline: Belarus leader picks loyalists to head courts.

text.p: Hardline Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko has appointed close allies to head the Constitutional and Supreme courts, further tightening his hold on the former Soviet republic.
Official newspapers published a decree on Sunday saying Grigory Vasilevich, 41, would head the Constitutional Court and Justice Minister Valentin Sukalo, 44, the Supreme Court.

The role of the Constitutional Court, which includes ruling whether presidential decrees and parliamentary laws comply with the constitution, is widely seen as symbolic after Lukashenko's won a referendum last November giving him sweeping powers.
Vasilevich has been a member of the old Constitutional Court until now and has sided with Lukashenko at a time of political controversy in the country of 10 million people.
Opponents describe Lukashenko as authoritarian but he has mustered popular support for his hardline rule in a country seeking identity after the collapse of the Soviet Union.

"I had no doubts that the new Constitutional Court would be headed by Vasilevich," Alexander Feduta, a leading political observer on the opposition newspaper Belarusskaya Delovaya Gazeta, told Reuters.
"He was the only judge who always backed Lukashenko -- sometimes he was alone in opposing the whole court when it ruled Lukashenko's decrees were unconstitutional."
Lukashenko signed the decree on Saturday.
The old Constitutional Court ruled 19 of Lukashenko's decrees unconstitutional, including one saying the November 24 referendum should have legal force and not just be consultative.
No international organisations have recognised the November referendum, which gave Lukashenko the right to prolong his stay in office beyond the year 2000.
Seven of the Constitutional Court's 11 judges, including its head, resigned last month in protest at Lukashenko's policies.
Sukalo, named to head the Supreme Court which rules on complicated criminal cases and oversees the legal system, is also widely regarded as loyal to the president.
As a member of Central Electoral Commission, Sukalo had backed Lukashenko's dismissal of Viktor Gonchar as head of the commission after he said the November referendum was illegal.
In another decree Lukashenko re-appointed Mikhail Myasnikovich as a chief of his administration.
